name: Recorded Future
group: Subsidiaries: technology companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Cybersecurity company collecting and analysing data from the open, deep and dark web to deliver threat intelligence.
capacity_detail: Acquired by Mastercard for USD 2.65bn in 2024
markets: Worldwide; offices in Boston, Washington DC, Gothenburg, London, Singapore and Tokyo serving enterprises and governments.
rationale: Global threat-intelligence brand selling to enterprises and governments; F1 data, cyber and hospitality audiences match its buyer profile.

name: Pismo
group: Subsidiaries: technology companies bought since Nov 2023
industry: cloud core banking and card processing
desc: Cloud-native issuer processing and core banking platform letting banks and fintechs launch payment and banking products.
capacity_detail: Visa completed its USD 1bn all-cash acquisition of Pismo on 16 January 2024
markets: Operations in Latin America, Asia-Pacific and Europe, serving banks and fintechs with cloud APIs.
rationale: B2B banking-platform brand courting banks across Latin America, Europe and Asia; F1 hospitality suits enterprise fintech sales.

name: Altium
group: Subsidiaries: technology companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Electronic design automation software company whose Altium Designer and Altium 365 tools engineers use to design circuit boards.
capacity_detail: Renesas agreed to acquire Altium for USD 5.9bn; completed August 2024
markets: Electronics engineers in the United States, Australia, China, Europe and Japan across automotive, aerospace and telecoms.
rationale: Engineering-software brand used in automotive and aerospace design; F1 engineering showcases fit its engineer audience and rival EDA sponsors.

name: Imperva
group: Subsidiaries: technology companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Cybersecurity software and services company protecting enterprise data and applications, owned by France's Thales Group.
capacity_detail: Thales acquired Imperva for about USD 3.6bn; completed 4 December 2023
markets: Worldwide enterprise customers for application, API and data security.
rationale: Cybersecurity brand competing with F1-sponsoring security vendors; F1 offers a global stage for enterprise security buyers.

name: SevenRooms
group: Subsidiaries: technology companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Restaurant technology company providing a cloud platform for reservations, bookings and guest data for restaurants and hotels.
capacity_detail: DoorDash acquired SevenRooms for USD 1.2bn in cash; closed 13 June 2025
markets: Restaurants, hotels and other hospitality venues; headquartered in New York.
rationale: Hospitality-tech brand selling to premium restaurants and hotels; F1 Paddock Club hospitality is a natural showcase.

name: NinjaTrader
group: Subsidiaries: technology companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Financial technology company offering futures trading software together with clearing and brokerage services.
capacity_detail: Kraken acquired NinjaTrader for USD 1.5bn on 2 May 2025
markets: Retail futures traders, chiefly in the United States, via trading software and brokerage.
rationale: Retail-trading brand whose audience overlaps F1's affluent fans; trading and broker brands are already common F1 sponsors.

name: Deribit
group: Subsidiaries: technology companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Cryptocurrency derivatives exchange specialising in bitcoin and ether options and futures, owned by Coinbase.
capacity_detail: Coinbase acquisition of Sentillia B.V. (Deribit) for USD 4.3bn (cash plus Coinbase stock), 14 August 2025
markets: Global crypto options and futures traders; Dubai-based.
rationale: Crypto-exchange brands are established F1 sponsors; Deribit could target professional traders via F1's global, affluent audience.

name: Dotmatics
group: Subsidiaries: technology companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: R&D scientific software company whose platform and tools such as GraphPad Prism and SnapGene serve researchers.
capacity_detail: Siemens acquired Dotmatics for USD 5.1bn from Insight Partners; completed 1 July 2025
markets: Used by 2 million scientists and 10,000 customers; 14 offices around the globe.
rationale: Scientific-software brand selling to pharma and research labs; F1 engineering and data stories suit R&D audiences, but fit is moderate.

name: Belcan
group: Subsidiaries: technology companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Supplier of engineering, supply chain, technical recruiting and IT services to aerospace, defence, automotive and industrial customers.
capacity_detail: Cognizant acquired Belcan for about USD 1.3bn in cash and stock; completed August 2024
markets: Over 10,000 employees in about 60 locations worldwide serving aerospace, defence, automotive and government sectors.
rationale: Engineering-services brand serving aerospace and automotive clients; F1 engineering credentials resonate with its customers and recruits.

name: AMI
group: Subsidiaries: technology companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Hardware and software company specialising in PC and server firmware such as Aptio, AMIBIOS and MegaRAC.
capacity_detail: Lattice Semiconductor acquired AMI for USD 1.65bn in cash and stock; completed 27 July 2026
markets: International firmware supplier to PC, server and data-centre hardware makers.
rationale: Low-visibility B2B firmware brand; F1 mainly useful for OEM hospitality, so relevance is limited.

name: Avid Technology
group: Subsidiaries: technology companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Technology company making Pro Tools, Media Composer and other media software and hardware for entertainment industries.
ownership: subsidiary of STG (Symphony Technology Group), a private equity firm
capacity_detail: Acquired by an affiliate of STG for USD 1.4bn in November 2023 and delisted
markets: Media and entertainment, music and broadcast customers worldwide.
rationale: Broadcast and music-production brand; F1's media production and entertainment crossover could showcase Avid tools to creatives.

name: Moveworks
group: Subsidiaries: technology companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: AI company whose platform uses natural language understanding and automation to resolve employee workplace requests.
capacity_detail: ServiceNow completed its USD 2.9bn acquisition of Moveworks in December 2025
markets: Large enterprises; clients include Autodesk and Broadcom.
rationale: Enterprise AI brand competing with F1-sponsoring AI vendors; parent already uses F1, enabling a sub-brand activation.

name: WNS
group: Subsidiaries: technology companies bought since Nov 2023
industry: business process management and AI operations
desc: Business process services company with 64 delivery centres, now operating as WNS, part of Capgemini.
capacity_detail: Capgemini acquired WNS for USD 76.50 per share, USD 3.3bn in cash; WNS announced closing of the acquisition
markets: 64 delivery centres in countries including India, the Philippines, the UK, the US, Poland, South Africa and China.
rationale: Large outsourcing brand (revenue USD 1.27bn FY2025) selling to global enterprises; F1 hospitality and AI-operations storytelling suit its sales.

name: Hornetsecurity
group: Subsidiaries: technology companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Cloud email security and Microsoft 365 backup company serving businesses through managed service providers and channel partners.
ownership: subsidiary of Proofpoint (itself owned by Thoma Bravo)
capacity_detail: Proofpoint completed its acquisition of Hornetsecurity for total consideration of USD 1.8bn (announced 8 December 2025)
markets: Operates in more than 120 countries, serving over 125,000 customers via 12,000+ MSPs and channel partners.
rationale: Channel-led security brand with 125,000 customers in 120 countries; F1 partner programmes could energise its MSP and reseller network.

name: Esker
group: Subsidiaries: technology companies bought since Nov 2023
industry: AI finance and customer-service automation software
desc: French software company automating order-to-cash, procure-to-pay and customer service processes with AI.
ownership: subsidiary of Bridgepoint (with General Atlantic and management shareholders)
capacity_detail: All-cash EUR 1.62bn tender offer for 100% of Esker by Bridgepoint and General Atlantic, completed with delisting 3 March 2025
markets: Global headquarters in Lyon and US headquarters in Madison; sales EUR 205.3m in 2024.
rationale: Mid-sized French SaaS brand growing in the US; F1 hospitality offers enterprise CFO-audience access, though budget is modest.

name: Optro (formerly AuditBoard)
group: Subsidiaries: technology companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Connected risk platform for audit, risk, infosec and compliance teams, founded in 2014 as AuditBoard.
ownership: subsidiary of Hg (independent wholly owned subsidiary of Hg)
capacity_detail: AuditBoard agreed to be acquired by Hg for over USD 3bn (May 2024); Hg lists Optro as a portfolio company partnered in 2024
markets: More than 2,000 enterprises, including nearly 50% of the Fortune 500.
rationale: Freshly rebranded GRC platform needs brand awareness among Fortune 500 executives; F1 offers rebrand visibility and hospitality.

name: Vizio
group: Subsidiaries: technology companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: American designer of televisions, soundbars and related software, owned by Walmart since December 2024.
capacity_detail: Walmart acquired VIZIO Holding Corp. for USD 2.3bn; completed 3 December 2024
markets: North America; televisions sold through Walmart, with the brand moving towards Walmart exclusivity.
rationale: Consumer TV brand; F1's growing US audience and streaming tie-ins fit, but a Walmart-only strategy narrows reach.

name: Domain
group: Subsidiaries: technology companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Australian digital property portal business behind the domain.com.au, commercialrealestate.com.au and allhomes.com.au websites.
capacity_detail: CoStar agreed to acquire 100% of Domain for A$3bn; completed 27 August 2025
markets: Australian residential and commercial property buyers, renters and agents.
rationale: Consumer property portal in Australia; Melbourne Grand Prix sponsorship could fit, though reach is domestic.

name: Bridge
group: Subsidiaries: technology companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Stablecoin platform company providing infrastructure for moving and accepting stablecoin payments, owned by Stripe.
capacity_detail: Stripe closed its USD 1.1bn purchase of Bridge in February 2025
markets: Businesses using stablecoin payments globally via Stripe and APIs.
rationale: Young crypto-payments brand under an F1-sponsoring parent; F1's crypto-friendly sponsor pool makes it plausible, but it may rely on Stripe.

name: TSYS
group: Subsidiaries: technology companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Payment processing company providing card issuer processing, merchant services and prepaid card services.
ownership: subsidiary of FIS (Fidelity National Information Services)
capacity_detail: FIS completed its USD 13.5bn acquisition of Global Payments' Issuer Solutions business (TSYS) in January 2026
markets: Card issuers and banks in North America, Europe and other regions.
rationale: Large B2B payments processor selling to banks; F1 hospitality suits bank-client entertaining, though consumer visibility is low.

name: Worldpay
group: Subsidiaries: technology companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Payments technology company processing card and digital payments for merchants, now owned by Global Payments.
capacity_detail: Global Payments completed the acquisition of Worldpay from GTCR and FIS in January 2026, valued at USD 24.25bn
markets: Merchants worldwide across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Global merchant-acquiring brand competing with F1-sponsoring payment firms such as Visa and Mastercard; F1 delivers merchant hospitality.

name: Andrew
group: Subsidiaries: technology companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Wireless infrastructure business making outdoor antennas and distributed antenna systems for mobile networks.
capacity_detail: Amphenol acquired CommScope's Outdoor Wireless Networks and DAS businesses, including Andrew, for USD 2.1bn in cash, February 2025
markets: Mobile network operators and venues worldwide.
rationale: B2B telecom hardware brand; F1 venue connectivity stories could showcase it, but direct sponsorship relevance is low.

name: NTT DATA
group: Subsidiaries: technology companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Japanese multinational IT services and consulting company, a wholly owned subsidiary of Nippon Telegraph and Telephone (NTT).
capacity_detail: Revenue JPY 4.64 trillion (USD 29.3bn) in FY2025
markets: Operations in Japan, the UK, US, Germany, Italy, India, Brazil, China and many other countries.
rationale: Global IT-services brand of 197,800 staff competing with F1-sponsoring IT firms; F1 supports its push for global brand recognition.

name: Illumia (formerly Transact Campus)
group: Subsidiaries: technology companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Provider of connected payment and commerce technology for higher education, healthcare and enterprise, formerly Transact and CBORD.
capacity_detail: Roper acquired Transact Campus for USD 1.5bn (7 August 2024); Illumia states it has been part of Roper since 2024
markets: Universities, hospitals and enterprises, chiefly in the United States.
rationale: Newly rebranded campus-tech company; F1 relevance limited, as buyers are universities and hospitals rather than consumers.

name: DX
group: Subsidiaries: technology companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Developer productivity platform measuring engineering effectiveness for companies such as Adyen, Dropbox, Vanguard and Booking.com.
capacity_detail: Atlassian agreed to acquire DX for USD 1bn (September 2025); acquisition completed January 2026
markets: Engineering organisations at large companies in the US and Europe.
rationale: Niche developer-analytics brand; parent already sponsors Williams, so a DX activation would ride Atlassian's F1 platform.

name: Press Ganey
group: Subsidiaries: technology companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Healthcare performance improvement and experience-management company measuring patient, employee and customer experience, owned by Qualtrics.
ownership: subsidiary of Qualtrics (itself owned by Silver Lake-led investors)
capacity_detail: Qualtrics acquired Press Ganey for USD 6.75bn including debt; completed May 2026
markets: Health providers and plans chiefly in the US; Forsta serves market research clients internationally; 41,000 organisations.
rationale: Experience-data brand targeting health systems and enterprises; F1 data storytelling fits, though core buyers are US hospitals.

name: Softchoice
group: Subsidiaries: technology companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Canadian IT solutions provider reselling and managing software, cloud and hardware for businesses in North America.
capacity_detail: World Wide Technology closed its USD 1.3bn acquisition of Toronto-based Softchoice in March 2025
markets: Businesses across Canada and the United States.
rationale: IT reseller brand selling to North American enterprises; Montreal and US Grands Prix hospitality could support customer entertaining.

name: Procare
group: Subsidiaries: technology companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Child care management software for attendance, family information and tuition billing, used by over 37,000 child care businesses.
capacity_detail: Roper completed its acquisition of Procare Solutions for about USD 1.86bn in cash on 26 February 2024
markets: Child care centres in the United States.
rationale: Domestic B2B childcare software brand; F1 fit is weak, as buyers are small childcare operators.

name: CentralReach
group: Subsidiaries: technology companies bought since Nov 2023
industry: autism and IDD therapy practice software
desc: SaaS and AI software for workflow and administration of ABA therapy for autism and related disabilities care.
capacity_detail: Roper completed its acquisition of CentralReach for about USD 1.85bn in cash on 23 April 2025
markets: Therapy providers, chiefly in the United States; used by more than 185,000 professionals.
rationale: Specialist healthcare software brand; low F1 relevance given its clinical buyer base.

name: AssetMark
group: Subsidiaries: technology companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Wealth management platform providing investment, technology and custody services to independent financial advisers.
ownership: subsidiary of GTCR, a private equity firm
capacity_detail: GTCR acquired 100% of AssetMark for about USD 2.7bn (USD 35.25 per share); closed 5 September 2024
markets: Independent financial advisers in the United States; over USD 180bn platform assets (June 2026).
rationale: Wealth-platform brand serving affluent clients via advisers; F1 hospitality could reward top adviser firms, mainly US races.

name: Shinko Electric Industries
group: Subsidiaries: technology companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Japanese chip-packaging company specialising in IC substrates, formerly a Fujitsu subsidiary, now owned by JIC.
ownership: subsidiary of Japan Investment Corporation (state-backed; about 80%), with Dai Nippon Printing (15%) and Mitsui Chemicals (5%)
capacity_detail: JIC-led buyout valued at JPY 684.9bn (about USD 4.71bn); JIC completed the tender offer, delisting expected mid-June 2025
markets: Global semiconductor supply chain customers for IC substrates and packaging.
rationale: B2B chip-packaging maker; F1 sponsorship unlikely beyond technology-partner storytelling for semiconductor customers.

name: Hollysys
group: Subsidiaries: technology companies bought since Nov 2023
desc: Automation control system solutions provider in China, with overseas operations in eight other Asian countries and regions.
ownership: subsidiary of Ascendent Capital Partners, a private equity firm
capacity_detail: Ascendent acquired Hollysys for about USD 1.66bn in cash (USD 26.50 per share); completed 25 July 2024
markets: China plus operations in eight other countries and regions in Asia.
rationale: Industrial automation brand mostly selling in China and Asia; F1 relevance is low beyond the Chinese Grand Prix.
